title: Infinity-categorical comparison over conservative forgetful functors
statement:
Use [def-coef-complete-algebroid] for universe and infinity-category conventions. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ be infinity-categories, let $U:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ and $V:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be conservative functors, and let $H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ be a functor supplied with a coherent natural equivalence $VH\simeq U$. Suppose $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal E$ admit all small geometric realizations and $U,V$ preserve them; geometric realization means colimit of a coherent simplicial diagram indexed by $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Suppose $F:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal E$ are left adjoints of $U,V$ respectively, in the sense of natural equivalences of mapping spaces, and write $e:1_{\mathcal B}\to UF$ for the first adjunction unit. For $b\in\mathcal B$, let $\alpha_b:G(b)\to HF(b)$ be the adjunct under $G\dashv V$ of
$$b\xrightarrow{e_b}UF(b)\simeq VHF(b).$$
If $V(\alpha_b):VG(b)\to UF(b)$ is an equivalence for every $b$, then $H$ is an equivalence of infinity-categories. Conservative here means reflecting equivalences; all adjunctions, units and comparison maps are coherent.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017) Corollary 4.7.3.16 and Remark 4.7.3.17, printed pp. 689-690; stronger geometric-realization hypotheses imply the split-simplicial hypotheses there. This is the comparison criterion cited as Corollary 4.7.4.16 in Haugseng Proposition 5.2 (older numbering). Online source read; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this homotopy-coherent theorem.

proof.text: For all mapping-space tests below, work in a universe containing the mapping spaces of $\mathcal C,\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ (for example $\mathcal U\prime$, with a further containing universe). Apply [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] with that universe as its small universe. The indexing category $\Delta$ remains $\mathcal U$-small; this changes no colimit-existence hypothesis on the given categories. First $H$ preserves every small geometric realization. Given $P:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ with realization $c$, let $z$ be a realization of $HP$ in $\mathcal E$. The cocone $HP\to Hc$ induces $h:z\to Hc$. The functors $V$ and $U$ preserve these realizations. Under the given coherent equivalence $VH\simeq U$, both $Vz$ and $VHc\simeq Uc$, with their displayed cocones, are colimits of the same diagram $UP$. Consequently $Vh$ is an equivalence: its map on every mapping space out of these colimits identifies with the identity of the limit of mapping spaces, by the colimit criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. The componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] allows the coherent equivalence $VHP\simeq UP$ to identify these diagrams. Conservativity of $V$ makes $h$ an equivalence. Hence the cocone with apex $Hc$ is colimiting. This argument only uses realizations indexed by the small category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$; it requires no arbitrary colimits in $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Agent argument with the colimit comparison used at the end of the proof of Corollary 4.7.3.16, printed p.690; universal mapping-space criteria supplied by the cited DAG nodes.

proof.text:
For each $b$, conservativity of $V$ and the hypothesis on $V(\alpha_b)$ imply that $\alpha_b:Gb\to HFb$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal E$. Fix $c\in\mathcal C$. Consider the composite
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(Fb,c)\xrightarrow{H}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(HFb,Hc)\xrightarrow{\alpha_b^*}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(Gb,Hc)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,VHc)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,Uc).$$
Under the adjunction $G\dashv V$, a map $Hf\circ\alpha_b$ corresponds to $VHf\circ V\alpha_b\circ\eta^G_b$. By the defining adjunct formula for $\alpha_b$ and naturality of $VH\simeq U$, this is $Uf\circ e_b$. Thus the composite is the given equivalence of mapping spaces for $F\dashv U$, with its coherent naturality. Since precomposition by $\alpha_b$ is invertible (precompose by its inverse), the actual map induced by $H$, $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(Fb,c)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(HFb,Hc)$, is an equivalence. This is a calculation with the specified adjunction equivalences, not merely a bijection of homotopy classes.

source.place: Remark 4.7.3.17 and the free-object comparison in the proof of Corollary 4.7.3.16, printed p.690; the displayed adjunct calculation is written here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-adjunction-free-simplicial-resolution] to $F\dashv U$ and to $G\dashv V$. Each adjunction is coherent by hypothesis; $U,V$ reflect equivalences, their source categories admit all small geometric realizations, and they preserve them. Therefore every $c\in\mathcal C$ has a colimiting coherent resolution $P_\bullet\to c$ with each $P_n\simeq Fb_n$, and every $a\in\mathcal E$ has a colimiting coherent resolution $Q_\bullet\to a$ with each $Q_n\simeq Gd_n$. The source objects $b_n,d_n\in\mathcal B$ are chosen degree by degree; we will use the coherent diagrams $P_\bullet,Q_\bullet$ themselves and do not assert that their arrows descend to arrows between these chosen base objects.

source.place: Proposition 4.7.3.14, printed p.689; the hypotheses here are stronger than its split-realization hypotheses.

proof.text:
The functor $H$ is fully faithful. Fix $c,d\in\mathcal C$ and use its resolution $P_\bullet\to c$ from step 3. The mapping-space colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] and step 1 identify the actual $H$-induced map with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,d)\simeq\lim_{[n]\in\Delta}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(P_n,d)\longrightarrow\lim_{[n]\in\Delta}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(HP_n,Hd)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(Hc,Hd).$$
The middle arrow is induced by the coherent transformation of cosimplicial mapping-space diagrams obtained by applying the functor $H$; its naturality holds for all arrows of $P_\bullet$. Each component is an equivalence by step 2, after conjugating by $P_n\simeq Fb_n$ and its image under $H$. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes it an equivalence of the entire diagrams. Applying its coherent inverse gives an inverse on limits by the limiting universal property. All limits here are small limits of spaces, which exist by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. If needed, take a larger ambient universe of spaces containing the specified mapping spaces; only the original small $\Delta$ is used as index, so no larger colimit in $\mathcal C$, $\mathcal E$, or $\mathcal B$ is required.

source.place: Agent mapping-space argument using the free resolutions of Proposition 4.7.3.14 (printed p.689); compare the Yoneda and cosimplicial mapping-space argument of Corollary 4.7.3.16, printed p.690.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal E_0\subseteq\mathcal E$ be the full replete essential image of $H$. By step 4 and [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image], the restricted functor $H_0:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E_0$ has a coherent inverse $K$ and a coherent equivalence $H_0K\simeq1_{\mathcal E_0}$. Fix $a\in\mathcal E$ and its coherent resolution $Q_\bullet\to a$ from step 3. Every $Q_n\simeq Gd_n\simeq HFd_n$ lies in $\mathcal E_0$ by step 2. As a full subcategory contains every simplex whose vertices it contains, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the entire simplicial diagram $Q_\bullet$ factors through $\mathcal E_0$. Composing that factorization with $K$ gives a coherent simplicial diagram $P'_\bullet$ in $\mathcal C$. Restrict the coherent equivalence $H_0K\simeq1$ along this factorization: this supplies $HP'_\bullet\simeq Q_\bullet$ as coherent diagrams, including every face, degeneracy, and higher compatibility. This is not a choice of unrelated objectwise lifts.

source.place: Agent lifting argument via the full essential image; Higher Algebra proof of Corollary 4.7.3.16, printed p.690, likewise lifts a whole simplicial diagram through a fully faithful Yoneda image. Essential-image inverse: Kerodon Theorem 4.8.4.1 (01JX).

proof.text: Let $c'=|P'_\bullet|$, which exists by the assumed geometric realizations in $\mathcal C$. Step 1 identifies $Hc'$ with $|HP'_\bullet|$. The coherent diagram equivalence of step 5 and the colimit mapping-space criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identify this with $|Q_\bullet|\simeq a$: for each testing object the induced limits of mapping spaces are equivalent, by applying the coherent inverse of the diagram equivalence. Thus every object of $\mathcal E$ lies in $\mathcal E_0$. A full subcategory on all vertices is the entire category, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to the fully faithful $H$ now gives a coherent quasi-inverse on $\mathcal E$ itself. Therefore $H$ is an equivalence, as required.

source.place: Agent completion of the free-resolution argument for Corollary 4.7.3.16, printed pp.689-690; no SGA route or geometric purity input is used.

proof_origin.place: Adaptation of Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 4.7.3.14, Corollary 4.7.3.16 and Remark 4.7.3.17, printed pp.689-690: prove preservation and full faithfulness directly, then lift a free resolution through the full essential image. lean.statement: theorem infinity_monadic_comparison {C E B : SSet.{v}} [Quasicategory C] [Quasicategory E] [Quasicategory B] (U : C ⟶ B) (V : E ⟶ B) (H : C ⟶ E) (hU : ReflectsEquivalenceEdges U) (hV : ReflectsEquivalenceEdges V) (eta : ((ihom C).obj B) _⦋1⦌) (eta_src : ((ihom C).obj B).δ 1 eta = diagramVertex U) (eta_tgt : ((ihom C).obj B).δ 0 eta = diagramVertex (H ≫ V)) (heta : IsEquivalenceEdge ((ihom C).obj B) eta) (hC : HasGeometricRealizations C) (hE : HasGeometricRealizations E) (hUr : PreservesGeometricRealizations U) (hVr : PreservesGeometricRealizations V) (F : B ⟶ C) (G : B ⟶ E) (aF : CoherentAdjunction F U) (aG : CoherentAdjunction G V) (hfree : ∀ b : B _⦋0⦌, IsIso ((SSet.hoFunctor.map V).toFunctor.map (freeAdjunctionComparison aF aG eta eta_src eta_tgt b))) : IsFunctorEquivalence H
lean.note: The canonical mate components are constructed by applying G to the specified first unit component and natural equivalence component, then composing with the G–V counit component in the homotopy category of E. IsIso after V is exactly the equivalence test of Remark 4.7.3.17; no arbitrary comparison is assumed. The existing coherent-adjunction node is added to stmt_deps solely to reuse its published structure; no model-category hypotheses are imposed. Realization and conservativity predicates are helpers of this comparison criterion.
